messages:
Mia: Quick design review request — trying to tighten up the Trace viewer header: placement of the correlation ID, primary CTA for exports, and some copy/a11y nits. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/trace-viewer
Sam: skimming — main convo points?
Mia: tl;dr: two proposals
Mia: 1) Keep correlation ID visible left of the trace title, and add a small 'Copy request ID' button next to it (icon + text). 2) Move export dropdown to the right-most slot, make 'Permalink' first item and 'Export JSON/CSV' second.
Ashley: I like the explicit "Copy request ID" copy vs just the icon. Less ambiguous for new users.
Ashley: Also want to try a reduced-weight label for the ID itself so it doesn't compete with the trace title.
Sam: implementation note — putting a button next to the ID affects responsive layout for narrow screens. We should probably hide the text and leave only the icon under 520px.
Sam: propose using visually-hidden text for accessibility instead of toggling the label entirely.
Priya: +1 on visually-hidden text. For screen readers the button should read: "Copy request ID 0x1234abcd". We should aria-live announce "Request ID copied to clipboard" on success.
Priya: Also contrast: the current ID text is too low contrast against the header bg. Need at least 4.5:1 for body text.
Mia: Good catch. Ashley — can we try the ID at 16px/600 and increase contrast in the next pass?
Ashley: Yep, will mock.
Devon: If we add "Copy request ID" to exports, make sure exports include the correlation ids in both JSON and CSV payloads. Right now CSV export strips correlation headers for size reasons.
Devon: We should have a checkbox in export modal: "Include correlation IDs (may increase file size)". Default: off for CSV, on for JSON.
Sam: backend-wise that's fine. We'll have to version the export endpoint so clients can request metadata fields.
Mia: UX question: should "Permalink" be the primary item in the export dropdown? My thinking: Permalink is smallest friction and most used for triage.
Ashley: I think yes — users often share a link in Slack/Zoom. Make it first and give it the chevron icon.
Priya: Accessibility for dropdown: ensure keyboard users can open with Enter/Space and that focus moves into the menu. Also ensure escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Sam: noted. Also we've had bug reports where the copy button is not reachable by tab order because it's after the title. Need to ensure DOM order matches visual order.
Mia: Good flag — DOM order should be: title, id, copy button, export. That keeps tabbing linear.
A11yBot: Automated check: header contrast low (AA fail), interactive targets under 44px (tap target too small). See https://a11y.report/123
Priya: For keyboard shortcut, what about a global `c` when the trace panel is focused to copy the id? Might be handy, but dangerous conflicts.
Sam: we can scope it: only when trace panel aria-expanded="true" and focus is inside the panel.
Mia: Sounds good. Add microcopy: tooltip text for copy button: "Copy request ID (shortcut: C)" but only show shortcut if we implement it.
Ashley: Microcopy suggestion instead of "Export JSON": "Download JSON (includes metadata)" and for CSV: "Download CSV (compact, IDs optional)" — more descriptive.
Devon: Agree on descriptors. Also we should add a tiny analytics event: export_initiated (format, include_ids: bool).
Priya: One more a11y nit: when the Copy button finishes, the tooltip shouldn't remain visible; use aria-live polite for the status and remove focus ring appropriately.
Mia: Great list. Action items:
Mia: - Ashley: update Figma: move copy button next to ID, update contrast and label weight, add responsive hide behavior. (due EOD Thu)
Mia: - Sam: ensure DOM order matches visual order, hook up keyboard shortcut scoping, add menu keyboard behavior. (PR next week)
Mia: - Devon: expose correlation id in exports and add endpoint flag + analytics. (est. 2w)
Mia: - Priya: sign off on a11y once prototypes ready. (will run with the dev build)
Ashley: I'll attach the updated frames when done.
Sam: quick Q — do we need a visible divider between title+id and action buttons? Right now it feels cramped.
Ashley: I'll try a faint divider and increased padding for actions.
Mia: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Devon: thanks — will review the export wording in the API docs.
Priya: I'll add test cases for screen readers and keyboard flows.
Mia: if no objections I'll finalize this as the design direction tomorrow and flag in the release notes.
Sam: no objections from me.
Ashley: lgtm.
Devon: lgtm.
Priya: lgtm.
A11yBot: Automated check queued for updated frames once Ashley uploads them.
